question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given in the table below. Find $\text{E}[2X+\sqrt[3]{Y}].$

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=8$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.6$ | $0.1$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with supports ${S}_{X}$ and ${S}_{Y},$ respectively, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability mass function with support $S={S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}.$ If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=2x+\sqrt[3]{y}.
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2X+\sqrt[3]{Y}] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}r(x,y)\,f(x,y) \\  & =(2\cdot 1+\sqrt[3]{1})\cdot f(1,1)+(2\cdot 1+\sqrt[3]{8})\cdot f(1,8) \\  & \,+(2\cdot 2+\sqrt[3]{1})\cdot f(2,1)+(2\cdot 2+\sqrt[3]{8})\cdot f(2,8) \\  & =3\cdot f(1,1)+4\cdot f(1,8) \\  & \,+5\cdot f(2,1)+6\cdot f(2,8) \\  & =3\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.2+5\cdot 0.6+6\cdot 0.1 \\  & =0.3+0.8+3+0.6 \\  & =4.7.\end{aligned}
$$
